clusters.name: Your grandfather Gordon's return, 1989–1994
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Gordon coming back into the family in early 1989, within the next few years: your late nights and difficulty sleeping; your move to Hollin Road with Desmond that autumn; your wrist injury stopping your playing in the first term at the conservatory, and the blow-up with your roommate Rafe; your low mood and loss of footing once your grandfather died in June 1991 and your mother was about to remarry; your absorption in fixing radios through that time; and your stung feeling about your father not knowing your work, which lifted as you found your drive again in Portugal in early 1994. clusters.name: Your grandmother Winifred's bowel cancer, 2001–2004

clusters.name: Your grandmother Lorna's death, 2008
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Lorna's death in January 2008, within the months after: your distance from your mother deepened over the summer at Alder Creek, where she pushed to visit and you kept the door shut; your cutoff from her when you moved to Marlow Sound for nursing school that September, a silence that held for roughly a year; and your aunt Imogen's stroke in January 2009, which touched your extended family around the same time. Your anxiety and distance rose and your functioning fell through these months.

clusters.name: Your marriage to Wren, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: Around your marriage to Wren in March 2017, within the next couple of years: your contact with your mother eased off slightly once Wren came along; your cousin Alice was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in October 2017; your sister Tara married and was expecting her first child; your aunt Imogen's memory loss worsened and she began lashing out; your job steadied and paid well, easing your strain, yet your anxiety rose as you felt you ought to be driving projects forward; you started a sleeping pill in October 2019 though sleep itself did not improve; and around Wren's mother's retirement party at the lake in late October 2019, Wren became swamped with one thing after another, you overfunctioned laying out a plan for her, and you had no sleep through the weekend and pulled back from the family gathering. Your anxiety and your partner's symptom and anxiety rose together through this time, with relationship shifts between you and toward your mother; your job's steadying marked a brief lift in the middle.

periods.name: the year I left home
periods.words: The first is the year I left home: I went off to the conservatory, hurt my wrist in the first term and couldn't play, dropped out and drifted at my mother's place, then spent a bleak spell at the community college shooting pool every night until an exchange in Portugal snapped me out of it and I tore through the rest of my coursework.

periods.name: the long slump, roughly ages 27 to 29
periods.words: The second is the long slump, roughly ages 27 to 29, when nothing at home felt right, I moved to Gull Harbour away from nearly everyone I knew, then followed Marisol to Fenwick, and when that fell apart I went under, a depression I only really climbed out of after nursing school.
